subject: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: SOW, SKU mapping, and cutover timeline
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@healthnova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: AWS Marketplace metering next steps

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team liked the latency numbers and the idea of model routing for our bursty traffic. Procurement asked me to follow up with a formal SOW and the SKU/entitlement mapping so they can run it through our internal billing system.

Can you share the most recent SOW (finalized pricing + go-live milestones) and a spreadsheet that maps HealthNova SKUs to AWS Marketplace SKUs and entitlement granularity? Also: do you have standard language for usage-based invoicing vs. Marketplace settlement?

We’re targeting a production cutover window the week of July 18 if that helps for timeline planning.

—Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform, HealthNova Systems
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@healthnova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering next steps

Sam —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Attaching: SOW_HealthNova_v2.pdf (includes pricing table, milestone dates, and acceptance criteria) and a first-pass SKU mapping (fulfillment-sku-mapping.xlsx). High-level notes: 

- We recommend using per-1000-token metering for interactive API calls and a separate per-concurrent-session seat SKU for model-backed managed workflows.
- Marketplace fulfillment will be handled via the SaaS entitlement flow; Redwood will emit the metering records and the Marketplace handles settlement. We provide a webhook backstop for usage events if you want to reconcile on your side.
- Pricing in the SOW assumes standard Redwood hosted inference. If you plan Dedicated or Private deployment we can add an addendum for reserved capacity.

Action items I propose:
1) HealthNova procurement to review SOW and redline by EOD Thu June 24.
2) Redwood to finalize SKU mapping and send a canonical CSV for your billing system by Fri June 25.
3) Joint cutover runbook review the week of July 11.

I’ve looped in Aditya (marketplace integration lead) and Ben (billing/ops) to own the SKU mapping and webhooks. Marissa from the fulfillment onboarding team will be support-cc’d once procurement signs the SOW.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the redlines.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: INTERNAL: Procurement checklist & mapping notes (HealthNova)

Kim/Ben — quick internal note before we finalize the canonical CSV. I pasted Sam's ask below for context.

> "Can you share the most recent SOW (finalized pricing + go-live milestones) and a spreadsheet that maps HealthNova SKUs to AWS Marketplace SKUs and entitlement granularity? Also: do you have standard language for usage-based invoicing vs. Marketplace settlement?"

A few technical constraints to keep in mind: 
- AWS metering events should include customer_id (marketplace entitlement id), sku_id, usage_quantity (tokens), and a usage_timestamp. Our fulfillment mapping needs to account for chunking large payloads into single metering records to avoid overcounting. I’ve attached a sample mapping template (fulfillment-sku-mapping.xlsx).
- For invoicing language: for Marketplace purchases, settlement is AWS -> Redwood. If HealthNova wants to invoice internally based on our metering, they should ingest our webhook payloads (we provide a signed HMAC payload). Ben, can you confirm the webhook retention window and whether we can provide a daily digest CSV for their ERP?

Marissa — please hold the onboarding slot for week of July 11 for a cutover rehearsal. I’ll also schedule a 45-min tech sync with HealthNova to walk through SKU edge cases (multi-model bundles, trial SKUs, and seat proxies).

Thanks,
Aditya
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@healthnova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@healthnova.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering next steps

Kim,

Thanks for the docs — I reviewed the SOW and shared it with our procurement team. A couple items from procurement/legal: 

- We’ve redlined the SOW to include a 60-day acceptance window for the first month of billing and a clause that requires Redwood to provide usage logs for any disputed invoices within 10 business days. Redlines attached as "SOW_HealthNova_v2_REDLINE.pdf".
- For SKU mapping: procurement wants explicit mapping for any bundled SKUs (we need to know how you’ll meter bundle components). The fulfillment spreadsheet is a good start but please include a column for "billing_entity" and "internal_sku_id" so our ERP can map to our Chart of Accounts.
- Pricing question: the SOW shows a per-1k token rate for generation calls, but our finance team needs to know whether cached/prefetch tokens are billed. Please add a line item that clarifies how cache hits are treated.

We uploaded the redlined SOW to DocuSign and routed it to Sam and me; the link is: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/12345-HealthNova-SOW. We expect procurement sign-off by Mon June 28 if the redlines are addressed.

On the operational side: please confirm the webhook signature algorithm (HMAC-SHA256) and the retention period for raw usage logs. Also can Redwood provide a daily usage digest CSV (SFTP or HTTPS pull)? That will simplify our reconciliation.

—Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Procurement & Vendor Ops
HealthNova Systems

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering next steps

Maria / Sam —

Thanks for the thorough notes and the DocuSign link. Quick answers and next steps:

- Redlines: we’ll review the redlined SOW and return a respond-for-signature by Fri June 25. Legal is okay with the 60-day acceptance window but will ask for a short exception text around the first-month invoice reconciliation; we’ll include the 10-business-day log request.
- Bundled SKUs: Aditya will add the "billing_entity" and "internal_sku_id" columns to the canonical CSV and add rules for bundle decomposition (how component usage is attributed).
- Cache billing: Ben — can you confirm: our standard approach is not to bill cache hits. We’ll add an explicit line item in the SOW clarifying that cached tokens are not counted towards billable usage; uncached generation tokens are billed as normal.
- Webhook and logs: we support HMAC-SHA256; retention for raw usage logs is 90 days. We can provide a daily digest CSV via secure SFTP or an authenticated HTTPS pull — I’ll have Ben share the SFTP host and credentials workflow in the tech sync.

Proposed timeline (so we’re aligned with your procurement target):
- Thu Jun 24: HealthNova returns redlines (or notes) — Redwood triages same day.
- Fri Jun 25: Redwood sends canonical SKU CSV + updated SOW for e-signature.
- Mon Jun 28: Target procurement sign-off.
- Week of Jul 11: Cutover rehearsal and runbook review.
- Week of Jul 18: Production go-live window.

Marissa will schedule the runbook rehearsal and I’ll set a 60-min tech sync for Thu Jun 24 to walk through bundle rules.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW_HealthNova_v2.pdf, fulfillment-sku-mapping.xlsx
